summary: This prescription has been written for the management of Type 2 Diabetes and Stage-1 Hypertension. It contains 4 medicines. ReportSaathi explains what each medicine is generally used for — always follow your doctor's instructions exactly.

medicines.name: Metformin
medicines.frequency_full: Twice Daily — after breakfast and dinner
medicines.plain_language_explanation: Metformin is commonly prescribed to help control blood sugar in Type 2 Diabetes. It works mainly by reducing the amount of glucose your liver produces. It does not cause low blood sugar on its own.
medicines.safety_note: Take exactly as written. Do not stop without consulting your doctor.

medicines.name: Amlodipine
medicines.frequency_full: Once Daily — in the morning after food
medicines.plain_language_explanation: Amlodipine belongs to a group of medicines called calcium channel blockers. It relaxes the walls of blood vessels, making it easier for your heart to pump blood and helping to lower blood pressure.
medicines.safety_note: Do not stop suddenly. If you notice swollen ankles, inform your doctor at your next visit.

medicines.name: Aspirin
medicines.frequency_full: Once Daily — after breakfast (NEVER on empty stomach)
medicines.plain_language_explanation: A low dose of aspirin helps prevent blood clots from forming in arteries. It is often prescribed alongside blood pressure and diabetes medicines to protect the heart.
medicines.safety_note: Always take after food. Tell your doctor immediately if you notice dark or tarry stools.

medicines.name: Vitamin D3
medicines.frequency_full: Every Sunday morning — take with milk
medicines.plain_language_explanation: Vitamin D3 is a supplement (not a prescription drug). It helps the body absorb calcium and keeps bones and muscles healthy. Many adults in India have low Vitamin D levels.
medicines.safety_note: Take only once a week as written — not daily.
